name: cheque-check
title: Cheque Check
description: Reads the date as written in the CTS boxes (so 31 November is caught), shows the safe deposit window under RBI's three-month rule with a warning on the disputed last day, catches stale January dates and two-digit years, and says when Positive Pay applies.

meta.stops: Cheque bounced as expired or post-dated
meta.summary: Reads a cheque date as written and shows the safe deposit window, so a cheque isn't presented after it expires, before its date or with a rejected correction.
catches: Impossible dates (31 November) and two-digit years
Cheques older than three months, or post-dated
A January cheque still carrying last year's date
Corrections other than to the date, which need a fresh cheque
Amounts where Positive Pay applies (₹50,000 and above)
limits: RBI doesn't define whether the three-month window ends on the same date or the day before; the earlier day is shown as safe
Your bank may make Positive Pay mandatory at a different amount
India rules by default; other countries need custom rules
a11y: Labelled date, amount and correction fields; aria-invalid and aria-describedby to the issues list
Focus moves to the first fix

sources.label: RBI FAQs on Cheque Clearing (7 Jan 2026)
RBI notification: validity of cheques reduced to three months (4 Nov 2011)

rules.note: Informational; check with your bank. Checked: three-month validity from the instrument's date; changes to payee or amount need a fresh cheque; Positive Pay enabled for ₹50,000 and above, banks may mandate it from ₹5,00,000.
